verses.text: Here are the names of Israel’s sons who came to Egypt with Jacob, each bringing his own family. 🧳
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah; 👥
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin; 👥
Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher. 👥
Jacob’s family had seventy people in all, including Joseph, who was already in Egypt. 🔢
Joseph died, then all his brothers, and everyone from that generation. 🕊️
But Israel’s people kept having children. They multiplied, grew stronger, and filled the land. 🌱
Then a new king took power in Egypt—one who didn’t know Joseph. 👑
He told his people, ‘Look, the Israelites are now more numerous and stronger than we are. ⚠️
‘Come on, we need to move smart. If they keep multiplying, they could side with our enemies in a war, fight us, and leave the land.’ 🗣️
So the Egyptians put taskmasters over them to crush them with forced labor. The Israelites built Pharaoh’s storage cities, Pithom and Rameses. 🧱
But the more the Egyptians oppressed them, the more the Israelites multiplied and spread out. The Egyptians grew afraid of them. 📈
The Egyptians forced the Israelites into brutal labor. ⛓️
They made their lives bitter with hard work—mixing mortar, making bricks, and doing every kind of field labor. They treated them ruthlessly in all of it. 💔
Egypt’s king spoke to two Hebrew midwives, one named Shiphrah and the other Puah. 👥
He told them, ‘When you help Hebrew women give birth and see a boy on the birth stool, kill him. If it’s a girl, let her live.’ ⚠️
But the midwives respected God and didn’t do what Egypt’s king ordered. They let the boys live. 🙏
Egypt’s king called the midwives in and demanded, ‘Why did you do this? Why did you let the boys live?’ 👑
The midwives answered Pharaoh, ‘Hebrew women aren’t like Egyptian women. They’re strong and give birth before a midwife can get there.’ 🗣️
God treated the midwives well, and the people kept multiplying and growing very strong. 🌱
Because the midwives respected God, he gave them families of their own. 🙏
Then Pharaoh ordered all his people, ‘Throw every newborn Hebrew boy into the Nile, but let every girl live.’ 🌊
